correctness.rationale: The mapped Laplacian has strictly convex inverse trace for all individual edge weights, forcing a unique dihedrally invariant optimizer. Exact Fourier and quotient block inverse traces yield the correct objective A_n/c+B_n/a+2 sum_k 1/(a+2b t_k). Rim probabilities saturate their stochastic constraint. A finite cyclic resolvent proves c_n tends to zero; its derivative plus a uniform low-mode domination estimate proves eventual a_n=1/n, the sharp quarter-power leaf scale and the explicit n^(5/4) second coefficient. The maximum-degree asymptotic is a separate elementary Fourier integral. A packaged independent matrix assembly matched the orbit formula in 389 finite checks; those checks are not infinite proofs.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Deleting all leaves from a helm produces a wheel; deleting the hub produces a cycle corona. An optimizer on either changed graph does not restrict to an optimizer on the helm because both the feasible stochastic row constraints and Laplacian spectrum change. The present three-orbit quotient, quarter-power leaf scale, and subleading coefficient are not logical consequences of either special-graph theorem.

value.rationale: The helm is a classical natural network with one global hub and one private terminal demand per rim state. The full-support optimizer has the surprising coexistence of exact hub saturation, asymptotically half-weight rim steps, and a quarter-power leaf edge probability. The spectral cost has a nontrivial second term and outperforms a natural maximum-degree stochastic baseline by a diverging order-sqrt(n) factor. This design fact is neither a textbook normalization nor an arbitrarily chosen finite parameter slice.
